History of Present Illness:
This is a ___ year old ___ male with history of 
?coronary artery disease (normal pMibi in ___, chronic 
bronchitis, chronic hyponatremia and recent admission for PNA, 
who presents with epigastric burning and CP x 2days. He 
describes it as travelling from his epigastric area to his 
mouth, and is associated with SOB but no other symptoms, no 
n/v/diaphoresis. He notes that he took a friend's prevacid and 
his symptoms improved. He also describes a bitter taste in his 
mouth. No relation to meals, and not exacerbated with laying 
flat. Reports has had this burning sensation for many months - 
acutely worse over past 2 days.
.
In the ED, his vitals were 97.2 55 112/60 16 95% 2L (97%ra). His 
physical exam was relatively unremarkable. His labs were notable 
for hyponatremia and anemia which are chronic, first set of 
cardiac enzymes were negative. EKG had PVC's but no ischemic 
changes. He received a dose of aspirin, and a GI cocktail 
improved his symptoms. He was admitted for ___.
.
On the floor, patient denies chest pain now or on admission; 
reports that this was more so a burning sensation which resolved 
with medications in emergency department. Denies sour taste 
currently. Reports that he is hungry and is anxious to eat. 
Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations. Denies 
nausea/vomiting, diarrhea, or constipation. Concerned about 
lesion on left face which he says had been there fore weeks.
.

(+) Per HPI
(-) Denies fever, chills, night sweats, recent weight loss or

congestion - though he reports that being by the window brings

or tightness, palpitations. Denies nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, 
constipation or abdominal pain. No dysuria.

cTropnT-<0.01...<0.01...<0.___ year old male with diagnosis of coronary artery disease but 
normal pMIBI in ___ and recent admission for pneumonia admitted 
___ with burning chest pain. Brief hospital course 
was as follows.

1. Atypical chest pain:  Patient has a known diagnosis of PUD 
and GERD and is followed by Dr. ___ in the gastroenterology 
department. Based on patient's description, EKG, and recent 
pMIBI findings chest pain appeared to be less likely cardiac and 
more likely reflux. Furthermore, he described improving 
symptomatically when he took his friend's omeprazole. On last 
discharge, he was prescribed lansoprazole and ranitidine but it 
is unclear whether he was following this regimen. Despite very 
low suspicion for cardiac source, patient was admitted to rule 
out a myocardial infarction. Three sets of cardiac enzymes were 
normal. No arrythmias were seen on telemetry. Patient was 
started on omeprazole and maintained on ranitidine. Patient was 
also provided Maalox for symptomatic relief. On discharge, 
burning pain was resolved; he was scheduled for a breath test to 
assess for H. pylori and close follow-up with Dr. ___.

2. Aortic stenosis:  Moderate (AoVA 1.0-1.2cm2). Maintained good 
blood pressure control with antihypertensives per home regimen.

3. Chronic bronchitis:  Without cough or shortness of breath 
during hospital stay. Continued Advair standing and albuterol, 
ipratropium as needed per home regimen.

4. Chronic hyponatremia:  Baseline is about 126-130, at 126 on 
admission; on day of discharge came up to 131. Did not 
aggressively intervene while inpatient. Previously thought to be 
secondary to SIADH.

5. Post-herpetic neuralgia:  Continue lidoderm patch as needed, 
per home regimen.

Home With Service

___

- GERD
- History of peptic ulcer disease

Secondary:

Hemodynamically stable. Ambulatory.
 
Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted on ___ for a burning sensation in 
your chest and mouth. You were hospitalized to ensure that you 
were not having a heart attack - you did not have a heart 
attack. We feel that the pain is due to reflux, also known as 
GERD. Dr. ___ has been treating your GERD as an outpatient. We 
made some modifications to your medications in the hospital 
which helped to control your symptoms.

Your medication regimen has changed. Please review your 
medication list closely. Changes include:
- Omeprazole, a medication that helps with GERD

Please follow-up with your appointments as listed below. In 
addition to following up with Dr. ___ in GI clinic, you will 
also have a breath test done to assess for H. pylori, a bacteria 
which can cause burning in your stomach.

Please return to the emergency department or call your physician 
for any chest pressure, shortness of breath, blood in your 
stools, or for any other concerns.
 
Followup Instructions:
